title: Maximum Median Sum of Subsequences of Size 3
summary: Given an integer array where the length is divisible by 3, you can remove any three elements at a time, compute their median, and remove them.
statement: Given an integer array where the length is divisible by 3, you can remove any three elements at a time, compute their median, and remove them. The goal is to maximize the sum of these medians. The median of a sequence of odd length is the middle element when the sequence is sorted.
constraints: nums length is divisible by three.
Partition all elements into triplets and sum each triplet’s median.
Return the maximum possible median sum.
hints: Reserve the smallest third as unavoidable low members, then take every second value from the remainder as a median.
Sum indices n/3, n/3+2, and so on.
Pairing each chosen median with one larger value and one reserved smaller value constructs the optimum.
editorial: Pairing each chosen median with one larger value and one reserved smaller value constructs the optimum.

tests.explanation: Triplets can have medians three and two, producing five.
The only triplet has median two.
